HIGH_HISTAMINE.mechanism: Bacterial histidine decarboxylase converts high free histidine in muscle tissue to heat-stable histamine under temperature abuse (>4°C). Cooking, freezing, or frying does NOT destroy histamine.

CIGUATERA_WATCH.mechanism: Bioaccumulation of lipid-soluble ciguatoxins (produced by Gambierdiscus dinoflagellates) up the coral reef trophic food chain to apex predators. Odorless, tasteless, and completely heat-stable.
CIGUATERA_WATCH.critical_factor: Reef carnivorous fish weight/size and origin reef health.

LOW_INTRINSIC_RISK.mechanism: Low free histidine and zero ciguatoxin risk. Primary risks are standard post-mortem bacterial decomposition (Pseudomonas, Shewanella) and illegal formalin (formaldehyde) dipping by unscrupulous vendors.
LOW_INTRINSIC_RISK.critical_factor: Visual eye/gill freshness and formalin sensory check.

UNKNOWN_RISK.mechanism: Species could not be identified with >= 0.70 confidence. Conservative screening applies.

tongkol.handling_advice: Must be packed in crushed ice immediately upon catch. Never buy if sitting at ambient market temperature without ice.
tongkol.symptom_warning: Flushing, throbbing headache, hives, itchy rash, oral burning, vomiting, diarrhea within 10-60 mins of eating.

kembung.handling_advice: High fat and histidine content makes it spoil quickly. Ensure gills are bright red and flesh bounces back firmly.
kembung.symptom_warning: Scombroid poisoning with rapid allergic-like histamine response.

cakalang.handling_advice: High metabolic rate pelagic species. Rapid histamine build-up if ice melts at the stall.
cakalang.symptom_warning: Severe histamine reactions often mistaken for acute seafood allergy.

tenggiri.handling_advice: Premium scombroid fish. Frequently bought for pempek or otak-otak. High risk if thawed and refrozen.
tenggiri.symptom_warning: Histamine toxicity with rapid onset facial flushing and palpitations.

kerapu.handling_advice: Predatory reef fish. Larger specimens (>2.5 kg) carry higher ciguatoxin concentration. Check eye/gill freshness and avoid exceptionally large reef specimens.
kerapu.symptom_warning: Ciguatera: temperature reversal (hot feels cold, cold feels hot), numbness in lips/fingers, joint pain lasting weeks.

kakap.handling_advice: Carnivorous reef/coastal fish. Gills must be bright crimson red and eyes clear and bulging.
kakap.symptom_warning: Potential ciguatera in warm reef specimens. Mild gastrointestinal and neurological symptoms.

bandeng.handling_advice: Low intrinsic histamine. Main threat is chemical preservation (formalin) to prolong shelf life in warm markets. Check for natural fish scent and firm but elastic flesh.
bandeng.symptom_warning: Bacterial gastroenteritis (nausea, cramping) or chemical mucosal irritation if formalin-tainted.

gurame.handling_advice: Freshwater fish commonly sold live or freshly slaughtered. Low chemical or biological toxin risk.
gurame.symptom_warning: Standard bacterial food poisoning if gills are muddy brown and slimy.

nila.handling_advice: Freshwater farmed staple. Spoilage shows quickly via eye sinking and gill mucus.
nila.symptom_warning: Bacterial foodborne infection if consumed deteriorated.

lele.handling_advice: Extremely hardy species, often sold alive. Inspect skin mucus and gill freshness if sold dead.

unknown.handling_advice: Species could not be verified automatically. Use manual selection sheet to verify if fish belongs to Scombridae family.
